title: District Commission's Obligation to Decide the Issue of Admissibility of the Complaint

content.scenario: A consumer files a complaint against a trader alleging unfair trade practices. The District Commission receives the complaint but fails to decide on its admissibility within the specified timeframe of 21 days.
content.outcome: The complaint shall be deemed to have been admitted, as the District Commission has not decided on the issue of admissibility within the specified timeframe.

user_queries: What happens if the District Commission does not decide on admissibility within the specified timeframe?
Can a complaint be deemed admitted if the District Commission fails to decide on admissibility?
What are the consequences of a complaint being deemed admitted?
